## Highlights

### Workflow Schedules 

Workflow Schedules is a durable server-managed scheduling primitive that replaces hand-rolled cron workflows. It supports overlap policies (Skip, Buffer, Concurrent, Cancel/Terminate Previous), catch-up on missed fires, jitter, backfill, and pause-on-failure. 

_What can the user do with it?_

Cadence Schedules let you run a workflow on a cron-based schedule without managing the timer yourself. You can pause and resume a schedule without deleting it, trigger past runs on demand via backfill, control what happens when a previous run is still executing when the next fire is due (overlap policies), and configure whether missed runs should catch up or be skipped when a schedule is unpaused.

_Why should the user use it?_

Before Schedules, recurring workflows required either a Cadence Cron (using ContinueAsNew in a loop) or an external scheduler. Schedules move that complexity into Cadence: the server owns the timer, handles missed fires, and gives you lifecycle controls (pause, backfill, delete) through APIs, SDKs, and the CLI without touching workflow code.

_What customers are using it? What is their use case?_

Machine learning platforms like [Michelangelo](https://github.com/michelangelo-ai/michelangelo) use Schedules to trigger training and scoring workflows on a recurring basis. Their primary requirement was the ability to pause a schedule during a lockdown or bug fix period without permanently deleting it, and to control whether missed runs should catch up or be skipped on resume.

_Who can use it?_

Any team running workflows on Cadence. Accessible via Go SDK, Python SDK, and the Cadence CLI. 

**Requirements**

Cadence Server >= [v1.4.1](https://github.com/cadence-workflow/cadence/releases/tag/v1.4.1)

**Links**

- [Concepts documentation](https://cadenceworkflow.io/docs/concepts/schedules) 
- [Go SDK](https://cadenceworkflow.io/docs/go-client/schedules)

### ⚠️ Metrics ⚠️ ###

Timer metrics are no longer emitted by default and is **replaced by** histogram metrics. See why https://github.com/cadence-workflow/cadence/issues/7741

### ⚠️ x/blocks API Removal ⚠️ ###

API is no longer needed since cadence-web now supports interactive query. See details https://github.com/cadence-workflow/cadence-go-client/pull/1496

## Highlights

### Workflow / activity APIs

#1495 GetActivityOptions — hooks/middleware can read current options instead of only overwriting them.
#1467 ResettableTimer — Reset() instead of cancel / handle CanceledError / start a new timer; replay-safe.
#1459 NewBatchFuture left experimental x for stable workflow (import break for x users).
#1447 HasActivityInfo — check activity context without panic/recover around GetInfo.
#1479 Maybe() on mocks — optional / fire-and-forget assertions.
#1451 Attempt number on activity (and local activity) logs.

### Active-active / domains

#1438 ActiveClusterSelectionPolicy on start options (nil-safe; server first). Also filled in missed CronOverlapPolicy mapping.
#1442 / #1446 Domain mappers for ActiveClusters / ActiveClustersByRegion.
#1461 / #1478 FailoverDomain — failover as a write-permission API, not admin UpdateDomain.
#1468 ListFailoverHistory and redesigned active-active IDL (breaks earlier RCs only).
#1469 / #1470 Public ActiveClusterSelectionPolicy and ClusterAttribute types.

### Client / query

#1445 / #1456 …WithOptions + QueryConsistencyLevel; STRONG reads the active cluster (higher latency on passive). Old methods unchanged.
#1490 Auto-forwarding flag — workers on a passive cluster can still poll/process when the server forwards.
#1486 cadence-caller-type: sdk so frontend can tell SDK vs other clients.
#1458 Request IDs on APIs that lacked them — idempotent retries, especially signals.

### Workers / sessions / metrics

#1449 Ephemeral session task lists (flagged); per-host lists go away when unused. Needs server TaskListKind or polls error.
#1460 Helpers/docs for experimental blocks Query UI.
#1489 Dual-emit timers as histograms (more series until migration ends).
#1437 Task-permit gauges → histograms for a real distribution.

# We are v1.0!

## What does this mean?!

At the moment, not much.  This is largely to mirror [the v1.0 release in the server](https://github.com/uber/cadence/releases/tag/v1.0.0).

Importantly, v1.0 _does not_ imply any change to backwards compatibility - the current policy is still "best effort with some obvious exceptions" (like new methods on the service client interface).  
Going by previous version patterns, this would have been labeled v0.20.0 as it is a relatively incremental change off of v0.19.1.

## Coming soon(ish): v2

**We are planning on releasing a v2 of this client!**  There will likely be more v1 changes first though.

v0 / v1 has been boxed in a bit by backwards compatibility requirements and a few leaky APIs (aliases, exposed thrift objects, etc).  This has been making some desired changes difficult or nigh-impossible.

Because of this, v2 is intended largely as a cleanup so we can make larger internal changes without interrupting our users.  We will be intentionally avoiding major semantic changes, and you will be able to _and encouraged to_ use v1 and v2 side by side to gradually migrate.  We'll be relying on this v1+v2 ability internally quite a bit, to migrate our monorepo :)
Workflow histories should remain backwards compatible, but code will require some simple and generally-obviously-correct changes, and previously-opt-in features may become opt-out or simply disappear in favor of the new behavior.

When this occurs, it will essentially signal the end of feature development on v1.  We will likely make exceptions for IDL changes (largely due to the shared IDL repository, which protobuf effectively requires us to use) and easily-backport-able bugfixes, but this will end at some point.
Due to this, you will definitely be _encouraged_ to migrate ASAP, so you can eliminate the v1 dependency.

We'll have migration details written up in detail when it's ready.

Of particular note:

The Yarpc upgrade should be safe for basically everyone, and it removes the need to pin `github.com/apache/thrift` to an old version - the required old version is now correctly inherited from Yarpc.  More details can be seen in Yarpc's PR: https://github.com/yarpc/yarpc-go/pull/2075
This _partially_ corrects a number of version-related issues, e.g. #523 , #812 , #1107 , and part of #1129 .  Since Go modules cannot prevent an upgrade, they cannot be stopped entirely, but it should prevent them from occurring for users who do not already depend on a newer thrift.

If you encounter test failures due to logic in `defer` running where it did not previously: your tests likely depended on the bug fixed in #1117 .  The behavior now matches production more closely, so please update your tests.

And last but not least: Selector and Channel docs are now significantly more detailed.  Please consider reading them!

**EntityNotExistError** will be returned if the workflow is not in the history. This could happen if the workflow never starts or the workflow completes and passes the retention days.
**WorflowExecutionAlreadyCompletedError** will be returned if the workflow is in the history and is completed.

Local activity is added to address the use case where a large number of activities are created on each decision task, and each activity is very simple and short lived, and they needs to be completed quickly.
Some key difference between local activity and regular activity are:
* Local activity is scheduled and run by the workflow worker locally.
* Local activity does not need Cadence server to schedule activity task and does not rely on activity worker.
* No need to register local activity.
* The parameter activity to ExecuteLocalActivity() must be a function.
* Local activity is for short living activities (usually finishes within seconds).
* Local activity cannot heartbeat.

## Breaking changes
* Upgrade client to thriftrw changes (#246)

Note: we switched RPC from directly using tchannel to yarpc. Part of that change is switching from using thrift to thriftrw to generate thrift client code (#246). This means the thrift client is now workflowserviceclient.Interface instead of cadence.TChanWorkflowService. Below APIs which used to require cadence.TChanWorkflowService are now requiring workflowserviceclient.Interface. Calls to those APIs will needs a proper update:
* cadence.NewClient(...)
* cadence.NewDomainClient(...)
* cadence.NewWorker(...)

To create a workflowserviceclient.Interface instance, you need a yarpc.Dispatcher. Below is a simplified sample code to do so:
```go
import (
  "go.uber.org/cadence/.gen/go/cadence/workflowserviceclient"
  "go.uber.org/yarpc"
  "go.uber.org/yarpc/transport/tchannel"
)
var _cadenceFrontendService = "cadence-frontend"
func createCadenceServiceClient() workflowserviceclient.Interface {
	tch, _ := tchannel.NewChannelTransport(tchannel.ServiceName(_cadenceFrontendService))
	dispatcher = yarpc.NewDispatcher(yarpc.Config{
		Name: "cadence-client",
		Outbounds: yarpc.Outbounds{
			_cadenceFrontendService: {Unary: tch.NewSingleOutbound("127.0.0.1:7933")},
		},
	})
	serviceClient := workflowserviceclient.New(dispatcher.ClientConfig(_cadenceFrontendService))
	return serviceClient
}
```
